description: Support package, not an SDK: install the SDK package first (VisioForge.DotNet.VideoCapture, VisioForge.DotNet.MediaPlayer, VisioForge.DotNet.VideoEdit or VisioForge.DotNet.Core) and add this one only when the deployment guide lists it. Xiph DirectShow filters for the VisioForge .NET SDKs on Windows x86: Ogg muxer/demuxer, Vorbis and Speex encoders and decoders, FLAC encoder and source, and the Visual C++ 2010 runtime.
releaseNotes:
* [ALL] New: an SDK running as a trial sends two anonymous events to `https://analytics.visioforge.org` - `trial_started` once per user account and `trial_expired` once when an engine first refuses to start after the trial; each carries only the engine name, SDK version and build, OS family and architecture and .NET runtime. An application whose licence covers what it uses never sends them; `VisioForgeX.Debug_Telemetry = false` or `VISIOFORGE_TRIALREPORT=0` turns them off.
* [ALL] Changed: every VisioForge Windows installer that sends the install report now shows a "Send an anonymous installation report to VisioForge" box on the licence page, ticked by default; clear it and nothing is sent (`INSTALLREPORT=0` for silent installs). The Unity package asks once per project before it sends its report.
* [Core] Changed: the DirectShow engines (`MediaPlayerCore`, `VideoCaptureCore`, `VideoEditCore`) no longer use LAV Filters. Playback defaults to `MediaPlayerSourceMode.FFMPEG`, IP cameras to `IPSourceEngine.Auto_FFMPEG`, and MJPEG/H.264 camera formats, `Memory_DS`, `MediaInfoReader`, thumbnails, frame grabs, picture-in-picture and Video Edit inputs go through the VisioForge FFMPEG source, so they need the FFMPEG redist (`VisioForge.DotNet.Core.Redist.FFMPEG.x64` / `.x86` / `.arm64`) instead of the LAV redist. The LAV and GPU source modes and LAV GPU settings are obsolete and select the FFMPEG path; set `Source_FFMPEG_HWDecoder` or `IPCameraSourceSettings.FFMPEG_HWDecoder` for an exact decoder. LAV Filters you install yourself still work through `Custom_Splitter` and `Custom_Video_Decoder`.
* [Core] Fixed: video whose width is not a multiple of 8 (such as 642x482) stopped with an error in `MediaPlayerSourceMode.FFMPEG`, and frame grabs of it failed; both work now.
* [Core] Fixed: the MAUI `SkiaVideoView` on Windows could throw or show a garbled frame after the video resolution changed during playback or capture.
* [Core] Fixed: on Android, a MAUI `VideoView`/`VideoViewX` removed from a page, or a disposed `VideoViewTX`, kept its video memory until the garbage collector ran; it is released at once now.
* [Media Blocks SDK .NET] New: `WebRTCSourceBlock` receives video and audio from a WebRTC sender; with `WebRTCSinkBlock` it makes a two-way video call between a .NET application and a browser with no media server.
* [Media Blocks SDK .NET] New: `EchoCancellationBlock` removes the far end's voice that the microphone picks up from the speakers in a call, with optional noise suppression and gain control (`EchoCancellationSettings`).
* [Media Blocks SDK .NET] Added: `VST3AudioBlock` opens the plug-in's own editor window on Windows, also during playback (`ShowEditor`, `CloseEditor`, `IsEditorOpen`), and raises `ParametersChanged` when the plug-in announces changed parameters (a preset loaded in its editor, parameters renamed or added, the plug-in reloaded), so the application can read `GetParameters` again.
* [Media Blocks SDK .NET] New: native Windows ARM64 support for the ElevenLabs blocks (`VisioForge.CrossPlatform.ElevenLabs.Windows.arm64`) and `RealSenseSourceBlock` (`VisioForge.CrossPlatform.RealSense.Windows.arm64`).
* [Media Blocks SDK .NET] New: camera controls on iOS - `SystemVideoSourceBlock.Camera2Controls` and `Capabilities` with the same members as on Android (zoom, torch, focus, exposure, white balance, stabilization); `VideoSourcesAsync` also lists the ultra-wide, telephoto and multi-camera devices.
* [Media Blocks SDK .NET] New: `VideoCaptureDeviceInfo.LensType` (`Wide`, `UltraWide`, `Telephoto`, `MultiCamera`, `Unknown`) on Android and iOS; on Android 9+ the lenses a phone hides behind one logical camera are listed as their own cameras. `VideoCaptureDeviceFacing.External` marks an external USB camera (Android, iPadOS), which Android listed as `Back` before.
* [Media Blocks SDK .NET] New: on iPadOS 17 and later an external USB camera is listed and keeps its own orientation, and plugging it in or out after `StartVideoSourceMonitorAsync` raises `OnVideoSourceAdded` / `OnVideoSourceRemoved`.
* [Media Blocks SDK .NET] Fixed: a live `VideoMixerBlock`/`AudioMixerBlock` with `IgnoreInactivePads = true` ended the stream before the first frame when every input started slower than the mixer latency; the mixer now starts at the first frame an input delivers. The same applies to the audio mixers of `MediaPlayerCoreX` and `VideoCaptureCoreX`.
* [Media Blocks SDK .NET] Fixed: `LiveVideoCompositor` sometimes showed no picture after a stop and a start.
* [Media Blocks SDK .NET] Fixed: on iOS and Linux, `DeviceEnumerator.VideoSourcesAsync` after `StartVideoSourceMonitor` raised `OnVideoSourceAdded` a second time for every camera, so a list built from the events showed each camera twice.
* [Media Blocks SDK .NET] Fixed: on iOS, calling `IOSVideoSource.Init` again left the previous capture session running and the camera on after `Stop`, and stopping a camera source broke an `AVCaptureDevice` the application held for the same camera.
* [Media Blocks SDK .NET] Fixed: on iOS, `IOSAudioSinkBlock` with mono or multichannel audio played nothing; it now plays mono to 7.1, downmixing where the route takes fewer channels. `CustomMixerSourceBlock` with 3 or 7 channels assigned them to the wrong speakers.
* [Media Blocks SDK .NET] Fixed: sources with an audio output connected but no audio in the stream - `UniversalSourceBlock`, `DecodeBinBlock`, `SRTSourceBlock`, `BluRaySourceBlock`, `RTMPSourceBlock`, `RTSPRAWSourceBlock` - showed only the first video frame or never started; the video now plays. `PreEventRecordingBlock` with only video connected now records without setting `AudioEnabled = false`.
* [Media Blocks SDK .NET] Fixed: `StopAsync` or `Dispose` during a `StartAsync` that was resolving the ONVIF address of a camera that never answers waited for the whole request timeout; both end the lookup at once now.
* [Media Blocks SDK .NET] Fixed: on Android, `FallbackSwitchSourceBlock` with an NDI main source failed to open with "Unable to create some pipeline elements".
* [Media Blocks SDK .NET] [Video Capture SDK .NET] [Media Player SDK .NET] [Video Edit SDK .NET] Fixed: a native Windows ARM64 application could fail to start on a machine without the Visual C++ ARM64 runtime; the ARM64 packages now carry it, and the x64 and x86 packages carry a newer Visual C++ runtime.
* [Media Blocks SDK .NET] [Video Capture SDK .NET] [Media Player SDK .NET] Fixed: on Android, Stop cleared only the first `VideoView` when a pipeline rendered to several; with several `VideoViewTX` views a size change reached the wrong renderer; and a pipeline started on a `VideoView` another pipeline was using drew into the same surface and could end the app - its start now returns `false` with an error.
* [Android] Changed: cameras are listed through Camera2 only; a device whose Camera2 service fails reports no cameras with an error in the log.
* [Android] Fixed: an external USB camera's picture turned with the phone; a camera whose format had no frame rate could drop below the reported rate in low light; a camera that opened after the 10-second timeout stayed open and blocked the next start.
* [Video Capture SDK .NET] Fixed: on a PC without the Visual C++ 2010 runtime, ASIO audio capture failed; the ASIO source filter no longer needs a Visual C++ runtime.
* [Video Capture SDK .NET] Fixed: `VideoCaptureCore` recorded no audio on the next capture after a preview, an animated GIF recording or a start without an audio device; a source without audio (IP camera, custom or push source) with the default audio flags failed to start or wrote an unplayable file; `Settings_Save` during a capture wrote the engine's audio flags instead of the application's.
* [Video Capture SDK .NET] [Video Edit SDK .NET] [Media Player SDK .NET] Fixed: `Settings_Load` of `VideoCaptureCore`, `VideoEditCore` and `VideoEditCoreX` returned `false` for every file, so saved settings were never restored, and `MediaPlayerCore.Settings_Load` left a hidden player window behind on every call. Window handles, bitmaps and views on nested settings objects must be set again after a load.
* [Video Edit SDK .NET] Fixed: `VideoEditCoreX` could crash with an access violation after the second or third render in a process; with `Output_VideoRotateFlip` at 90/270 degrees or `Output_VideoCrop` it cut off part of the picture; with the default H.264 encoder on an NVIDIA GPU it never finished a timeline holding a 24-bit PNG.
* [Media Player SDK .NET] New: `MediaPlayerCore` plays files natively in a Windows ARM64 application with `MediaPlayerSourceMode.FFMPEG` through the new `VisioForge.DotNet.Core.Redist.FFMPEG.arm64` package; the FFMPEG Source DirectShow filter installer also comes as an ARM64 setup.
* [Media Player SDK .NET] Fixed: `MediaPlayerCore.IsFileCrypted` kept the file locked or threw when it could not open the file or apply the key; it now releases the file and returns `false`.
* [Windows] Fixed: a Video Effects Pro Pan or Fade In/Out effect with equal start and stop times (the default) could leave the frame wrong.
* [All-in-One Media Framework (Delphi/ActiveX)] Fixed: the Delphi 13 packages did not install from the setup (the IDE asked for `.pas` sources); the setup now installs the precompiled package for every Delphi from 6 to 13 with the 32-bit and, from XE2, 64-bit library paths, and no longer installs IDE state and backup files.
* [All-in-One Media Framework (Delphi/ActiveX)] Fixed: on a PC with a broken 32-bit Windows Media Format runtime, an application with `TVFVideoCapture` or `TVFVideoEdit` could crash at startup; uninstalling one redist while another stayed installed left its `PATH` entry, registry key and folder behind.
* [Demos] New: WebRTC Video Call Demo (Media Blocks SDK, WPF) - a video call with a browser, with echo cancellation, mute and camera off.
* [Demos] New: WebRTC WHIP demo (Media Blocks SDK, WinForms) and a short console sample that streams a camera to browsers over WebRTC.
